label: Fire Records
release_notes: Second live album from the Melbourne band, recorded over three nights of a sold-out residency at TV Eye in New York. All eight tracks are live versions of earlier songs, plus a cover. Follows the first live album, Inflatable Graveyard.
Lineup: Gareth Liddiard - guitar, vocals; Fiona Kitschin - bass, vocals; Erica Dunn - guitar, keyboards, vocals; Lauren Hammel - drums.

Lineage: Liddiard and Kitschin come from the Melbourne rock band The Drones, and TFS formed when the two took a break from it. Dunn also plays in Mod Con, Harmony and Palm Springs; Hammel drums in High Tension.

Song sources: Fairyland Codex (2025) for tracks 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6; Braindrops (2019) for track 5; the debut A Laughing Death in Meatspace (2018) for track 7. Track 8 is a cover of The Saints, the 1970s Brisbane punk band. The studio albums are credited as written and produced by the band.
draft_comment: Live art-punk, noise-rock and psych-blues from Melbourne, caught over three nights in New York with The Saints thrown in for good measure. Say TFS on air (the band's own shorthand; the full name is an FCC word), and tracks 1, 2 and 7 are FCC too.

tracks.title: Irukandji Syndrome
tracks.notes: Studio version: snide talk-sung lead over bright three-part harmonies from Kitschin and Dunn, kinetic bass and busy drums (Fairyland Codex reviews). Live, it opens into a long guitar solo in the manner of The Velvet Underground's "I Heard Her Call My Name" (Fire Records)

tracks.title: Bloodsport
tracks.fcc: FCC “cunts” x1 (late in song, about line 35 of 48; Genius posts no sections; studio lyrics)
tracks.notes: Shortest track. Groove-fueled with punchy, stuttering guitar breaks and a funk-inflected Talking Heads feel; one critic hears surf rock. Kitschin and Dunn vocals are featured (Fairyland Codex reviews)

tracks.title: Goon Show
tracks.fcc: CAUTION “assholes” x1 (early in song, about line 6 of 40; Genius posts no sections; studio lyrics)
tracks.notes: Studio ~99 BPM (Shazam). Slow, foreboding march with a demented guitar solo, percussive and syncopated lead vocal, chorus harmonies that snap (The Needle Drop)

tracks.title: Stepping on a Rake
tracks.notes: Ballad: gently plucked guitar over sparse drums, tender and folk-like in the studio version, with heavier undertones live (Fairyland Codex reviews; Fire Records). Dire, sparse guitar backdrop

tracks.title: Who’s My Eugene?
tracks.notes: Studio ~84 BPM (Shazam, Chordify). Restrained, funky groove, called a Martian funk jam, with a cooing female lead vocal (Treble, DIY; sources differ on whether Dunn or Kitschin sings)

tracks.title: Moscovium
tracks.notes: Longest track. Slow build in a heavy, sinking minor key to a noisy peak with shouted vocals and guttural, warzone-like guitar (Cyclic Defrost, studio version). Sounds more urgent live (Fire Records)

tracks.title: You Let My Tyres Down
tracks.notes: Studio ~133 BPM (SongBPM). Huge, fuzzed-out, noisy guitar riffs with a loping, shambling feel, a boozy early Nick Cave vibe (reviews of the studio version)

tracks.title: This Perfect Day
tracks.notes: Cover of The Saints' "(This) Perfect Day" (written by Chris Bailey and Ed Kuepper, 1977). The Saints' original is raw, fast 1970s Australian punk with buzz-saw guitars

sources: https://tinnitist.com/2026/10/15/albums-of-the-week-tropical-fuk-storm-inflatable-graveyard-vol-2/ (repeats the press release; no independent review found, so no pull quote)

Lyrics screened on Genius (counts only): tracks 1 to 8, using the studio versions' lyrics pages (Fairyland Codex, Braindrops, A Laughing Death in Meatspace and The Saints) because Genius lists the live versions as unreleased. Live ad-libs and banter are not covered.
